diagnostics.message: aws_iam_instance_profile.elasticsearch references only aws_iam_role.elasticsearch.name, so it is created in parallel with aws_iam_role_policy.elasticsearch. The node launch configurations/ASGs consume the instance profile, but nothing orders the ec2:DescribeInstances policy attachment before the instances boot; instances can come up without the permissions the Elasticsearch EC2-discovery plugin needs. Add depends_on on the profile (or the launch configurations) so the policy is attached first.

aws_iam_instance_profile.elasticsearch is not ordered after aws_iam_role_policy.asg_discover. Master/data nodes use the autoscaling:DescribeAutoScalingGroups permission for ASG-based node discovery, but the profile can be used by the launch configurations before this policy is attached, so new nodes may start without the ability to enumerate the ASG.

aws_autoscaling_group.master_nodes launches EC2 instances into the cluster subnets that rely on the EC2 interface endpoint (private_dns_enabled) for API calls during Elasticsearch node discovery, but the ASG has no dependency on aws_vpc_endpoint.ec2. Interface endpoints create their ENIs/private DNS asynchronously, so instances launched in parallel can boot before the endpoint is ready and fail to resolve/describe the EC2 API. Order the ASG after the endpoint.

aws_instance.bootstrap_node is the seed node that runs the cluster-bootstrap user data and immediately queries the EC2 API for discovery, yet it is not ordered after aws_vpc_endpoint.ec2. Since the interface endpoint's ENIs/private DNS are provisioned asynchronously, the bootstrap instance can start before the endpoint is available and fail to reach the EC2 API. Add a dependency on the endpoint.
